description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of tasks across various linguistic families, with the vertical axis listing the categories—IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque—in descending order of task count, and the horizontal axis labeled '# tasks,' ranging from 0 to 80 with tick marks at intervals of 10. IE-Slavic has the highest number of tasks, approximately 80, followed by IE-Romance at around 45 tasks. IE-Germanic and Uralic both show task counts exceeding 40, with IE-Germanic at approximately 45 and Uralic at approximately 20. IE-Baltic has fewer than 15 tasks, and Basque, the smallest category, has fewer than 10 tasks. The chart visually emphasizes the steep decline from IE-Slavic to IE-Baltic, while the remaining categories show a more gradual decrease in task counts. Each bar is colored distinctly: IE-Slavic is light blue, IE-Romance is dark blue, IE-Germanic is light green, Uralic is dark green, IE-Baltic is pink, IE-other is red, IE-Indic is orange, Semitic is brown, Turkic is light purple, and Basque is dark purple. The bars are not sorted alphabetically but are arranged in descending order of their values, with no additional visual emphasis such as shading or bolding beyond the inherent color coding.
